subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Five Eyes Alliance
description: A fast breakdown of Five Eyes Alliance for builders.

hook.text: Five countries share intelligence so freely that they effectively spy on each other's citizens.

buildup.text: The US, UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand formed Five Eyes during World War II to share signals.

discovery.text: Each country can legally surveil non-citizens. So they trade data and bypass domestic privacy laws.

twist.text: Your own government can't spy on you. But a partner country can — and then share the results.

climax.text: Five Eyes shows that international alliances can create surveillance gaps no single law can close.

punchline.text: Can't spy on your own people? Ask a friend.

quiz.question: How does the Five Eyes alliance bypass domestic privacy laws?
options: Each country spies on the others' citizens and shares the data
They use diplomatic immunity to avoid all laws
They only operate in international waters
